headline: A US judge told a hearing he is likely to grant Apple an injunction in its trade secrets fight with OpenAI, which denies the claims.
score_reason: Kept at pool score: significant hearing signal, but no ruling yet.
importance_line: A ruling for Apple could restrict OpenAI's work on its first consumer devices, and it affects both companies and engineers who move between them, though the judge has not yet decided.
summary: Bloomberg reports that at a San Jose hearing on 14 Oct 2026 in Apple's lawsuit, filed in July, accusing OpenAI of conspiring to get confidential information from former Apple employees, US District Judge Edward Davila said he was "highly likely" to bar those former employees now at OpenAI from using Apple's proprietary information, but called a proposed forensic search of devices a "huge ask". OpenAI denies the claims and said just before the hearing that a former employee who returned to Apple had sent over a hundred confidential OpenAI files to personal accounts; on 13 Oct TechCrunch reported that the judge had ordered OpenAI to hand over hiring records in the case.
notes: Bloomberg page blocked; Bloomberg text read on Claims Journal (url). Apple filed suit in July 2026 (exact day not stated).
